children: Smith & Wesson Brands shares rose after the company posted higher quarterly sales.
The stock gained 10% to $13.50 in after-hours trading Thursday. Through the close, shares were up 23% this year.
The firearms manufacturer said sales jumped 32% to $112.6 million in the fiscal first quarter.
Profit was $2.6 million, or 6 cents a share, compared with a loss of $3.4 million, or 8 cents a share, in the year-ago quarter.
Smith & Wesson is seeing continued solid demand for its products in both the consumer and professional channels, Chief Executive Mark Smith said.
"With this momentum, we expect our second quarter to significantly outperform last year on both the top and bottom lines," Smith said.
The company expects a normal season environment and strong demand continuing into the second quarter. Sales are expected to rise 10% in the second quarter, and 5% to 7% for the full year.
